name: Muthoot Finance Ltd
title: Muthoot Finance Ltd - 533398 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Muthoot Finance Q4 FY26: gold AUM at record INR 1,65,000 crore and yields up ~50bp on pricing, but management gives no supply-side discipline signal and competition from new AAA-funded entrants is dismissed rather than quantified.

triggers.quote: Last quarter, we increased our rates by about 0.5% to 1% over certain types of loans. So, that is why we see the yield has gone up.

triggers.quote: a bunch of all AAA rated NBFCs who are themselves deep pocketed, can raise liabilities at finer rat es than us.

triggers.label: Tonnage falling as gold prices rise
triggers.quote: whenever gold prices go up, the tonnage will come down.

triggers.label: Standalone AUM growth guide ~15%
triggers.quote: Always in the first quarter, we have always been giving a guidance of 15% only.

summary.headline: Muthoot Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated AUM hit INR 1,81,916 crore (+49% YoY) and consolidated PAT INR 10,607 crore (+98%), with yield lifted to 20.76%.
summary.overview: Management reported record gold loan AUM, with standalone gold loan book at INR 1,64,000 crore and standalone PAT of INR 10,134 crore (+95% YoY). Reported yield rose to 20.76% from 20.34% in Q3, helped by about INR 85 crore of one-off income (auction INR 50 crore, ARC INR 35 crore) and a 0.5-1% pricing increase on certain loan types. Customer count fell about 2% and loan count about 3%, which management attributed to churn from small-ticket customers. Stage 3 assets rose on RBI-mandated borrower-level classification; management said stage 3 LTV including interest is about 57-58%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.35% in March 2025 (absolute rise due to borrower-level classification)
14th consecutive year of dividend since 2011 IPO

segments.name: Muthoot Finance standalone (gold loans)
segments.commentary: Loan book INR 1,64,000 crore with record standalone PAT of INR 10,134 crore (+95% YoY). Customer count down about 2% and loan count down about 3% due to churn in small tickets.

segments.name: Belstar Microfinance
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency 99.85% (vs 99.16% last year). Disbursed INR 7,500 crore (vs INR 6,000 crore). Opened 81 gold loan branches in the year; total branches including microfinance at 1,300.

segments.name: Muthoot Home Finance
segments.commentary: Loan AUM INR 3,485 crore (vs INR 2,900 crore, +17%). Interest income +36%, PAT INR 45 crore, GNPA 2.63% and NNPA 1.94%.

segments.name: Muthoot Money
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 9,794 crore (vs INR 3,900 crore, +151%). PAT INR 338 crore (vs INR 12 crore). Total income INR 1,294 crore, capital base INR 2,357 crore after INR 1,000 crore infusion, customers 4.6 lakh (from 2.74 lakh). CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to AA+ stable.

segments.name: Unsecured personal loans (standalone)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of about INR 4,000 crore, mainly cross-sold to the existing gold loan base; management said it is performing well, though no quarterly figure given for the increase.

guidance_outlook: Standalone AUM growth guidance of 15% for the first quarter, the usual practice for the past 10 years; to be revisited after Q1 or Q2.
Branch additions of about 200-300 gold branches at Muthoot Finance in FY27 (vs about 170 in FY26), and about 200 gold branches at Belstar.
No margin or profit guidance given; management said profit should grow with AUM.
Management expects borrowing costs to rise, so yields may be held at current levels rather than reduced further.
Yield sustainability: management declined to commit to the current 20%+ yield, calling the loans short-term and the pricing flexible.
capex_capacity: Plan to open about 200-300 gold branches at Muthoot Finance in FY27 versus about 170 added in FY26.
Belstar to add about 200 gold branches, from a base of about 100.
Muthoot Money branch expansion not aggressive for now, as branches are young and management wants them to mature first.
Gold loan AUM per loan account rose about 48-49% YoY at both Muthoot Finance and Muthoot Money; average ticket size cited at about INR 1,30,000 (vs INR 1 lakh previously).
demand_pricing: Competition: management said new AAA-rated NBFC entrants with lower cost of funds are not focused gold loan players and will face operational challenges; attrition is nil and staff count is about 30,000.
Tonnage: management attributed the tonnage decline to LTV resets on each four-month churn cycle, where borrowers now pledge less gold for the same loan amount.
Customer mix: about 15 lakh customers lost in sub-INR 30,000 tickets, offset by growth in INR 50,000, 1 lakh and 2 lakh tickets; loans above INR 3 lakh are 32% of the book.
Pricing: rates raised by 0.5-1% on certain loan types in the last quarter; management said yields may move up or down and it did not commit to the current level.
Gold import curbs: management said Muthoot does not finance bullion or coins and sees no direct impact; about 25,000-30,000 tonnes of household gold is held as collateral (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield increase inclusive of one-off recoveries and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-offs were about INR 85 crore (auction INR 50 crore, ARC INR 35 crore). Q3 included about INR 500 crore of interest recovery from GNPA, which is not in Q4. Management attributed the core increase to pricing on higher-gold-price disbursements and did not commit to sustaining the yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stage 2 and stage 3 assets rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly due to RBI-mandated borrower-level (rather than loan-level) classification. Stage 3 percentage is 2.34% vs 3.35% a year earlier. Management said stage 3 LTV including interest is about 57-58%, and that gold loans, not non-gold, drove the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count is down about 2% while acquisition is up; is there high-value customer leakage to competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said losses were concentrated in sub-INR 30,000 tickets (about 5 lakh under INR 10,000 and about 8 lakh in INR 10,000-30,000), offset by higher-ticket additions. It described this as normal churn in a mature portfolio, not competitive loss.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut rates to win customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has different schemes at 12-23% yields and will step up lower-yield lending when needed, but sees no need now. Median-term ROI guidance of around 3.5% was referenced.

qa_highlights.question: AUM guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone AUM guidance of 15%, given in Q1 as always; to be reviewed after Q1 or Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up gold lending in a subsidiary (Muthoot Money) rather than expanding the parent after RBI approval requirements were removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to explain and said it is a board decision for the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: How does the new RBI LTV framework affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has always followed RBI LTV limits, and the new framework allows up to 85% on EMI products. It is building software and has rolled out some products, with strategy to be reviewed after Q1.

risks_watch: Yield sustainability: about 85 crore of Q4 one-offs and a 0.5-1% rate hike drove the 20.76% yield; management said rates can be cut at any time and borrowing costs are expected to rise.
Competition from well-funded new gold lenders and a possible further fall in customer count and tonnage.
Stage 3 classification shift under RBI borrower-level norms; the absolute NPA increase may continue to show in the next quarter.
Gold price-driven LTV and tonnage resets, and the RBI LTV framework (up to 85% for EMI products) which is being implemented.
Whether the 15% AUM guidance is revised at Q1 or Q2, and whether the 200-300 branch plan is delivered.
Sustainability of rapid AUM-per-account growth (~48-49% YoY), which management attributed to gold price increases and higher ticket sizes; analysts questioned it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, but evasive on yield sustainability, pricing strategy, competitive dynamics and the Muthoot Money structure. Management repeatedly declined to give specifics and deferred decisions to later quarters.
key_quotes: Because we do not finance any gold purchase, we do not finance any gold bullion, etc., it actually does not affect Muthoot.
It is not because of any impairment in the loan, etc.. It is only because of the regulatory guidance that it should be shown as an NPA.
So, we don't want to give a view that the same rates will continue.
Always in the first quarter, we have always been giving a guidance of 15% only.

adds.what: 200-300 gold loan branches at Muthoot Finance in FY27 (vs ~170 added in FY26)
~200 gold loan branches at Belstar Microfinance (from base of ~100)

growth.why: Management guides ~15% standalone AUM growth for FY27 (to be revisited after Q1/Q2), backed by 200-300 new Muthoot gold branches and ~200 Belstar branches, though no profit guidance and tonnage is falling while ticket size rises (~INR 1.3 lakh) and the quarter's yield was lifted by ~INR 85 crore of one-off income.
